locator: ISO landing page — abstract, general information, life cycle
evidence_summary: ISO 9241-11:2018 applies the usability framework to interactive and other systems, industrial and consumer products, and services; Edition 2 is published and was confirmed in ISO's 2023 systematic review.
limitations: The official landing page is metadata/abstract, not the full normative text; it does not prescribe specific evaluation methods.

locator: ISO OBP reuse of ISO 9241-11:2018, 3.1.15; ISO 9241-220/115 terminology pages
evidence_summary: ISO 9241-11 defines context of use as the combination of users, goals and tasks, resources, and environment; environment includes technical, physical, social, cultural and organizational environments.
limitations: The definition is re-published in ISO OBP pages for related standards; it is not a complete operational checklist or a review-claim schema.
notes: SOURCE FACT; same ISO 9241 origin chain as R03-S01, not separately counted for strength.

evidence_summary: A user is a person who interacts with a system, product or service; a user group is a subset of intended users differentiated by characteristics of users, tasks or environments that could influence usability.
limitations: This does not define an opinion holder, a demographic taxonomy, or which characteristic belongs on an individual review claim.

evidence_summary: ISO 9241-11 defines a goal as an intended outcome and a task as a set of physical, perceptual and/or cognitive activities undertaken to achieve a specific goal; goals are independent of means while tasks describe particular means.
limitations: The source makes activity a constituent of task; it does not establish a universally separate Activity entity layer for product-review claims.

locator: ISO OBP terminology, ISO 9241-11:2018 usability definition
evidence_summary: Usability is the extent to which specified users achieve specified goals with effectiveness, efficiency and satisfaction in a specified context of use.
supports: evaluation applicability depends on specified context
condition mismatch is relevant before comparison
limitations: The definition does not provide a conflict/contradiction algorithm for two external review claims.

locator: ISO landing page — abstract and general information
evidence_summary: ISO 9241-210:2019 is the current confirmed human-centred design standard for life-cycle principles and activities for computer-based interactive systems, addressing hardware and software components.
supports: context analysis as HCD input boundary
limitations: The public abstract does not expose a complete context-of-use field model; ISO 9241-210 is not used here as a test protocol source.

locator: ISO landing page — abstract, status and life cycle
evidence_summary: ISO/IEC 25063:2014 specifies high-level and detailed context-of-use descriptions for existing, intended, implemented or deployed systems; its abstract names users and stakeholder groups, characteristics of user groups, user goals, user tasks and environments. ISO lists it as published, with ISO/FDIS 25063 in Final Draft International Standard approval phase / replacement pending.
limitations: The full standard is paywalled and the pending revision means this edition cannot be treated as an immutable current checklist.
notes: SOURCE FACT; current status recorded separately from 2014 publication date.

evidence_summary: ISO/IEC 25063's published preview describes historical context of use as users, tasks, equipment (hardware, software and materials), and physical and social environments; it says equipment is described as part of the technical and technological environment.
limitations: This is ISO/IEC 25063's 2014 definition derived from ISO 9241-11:1998, not the current ISO 9241-11:2018 wording; it does not resolve whether a companion device is a product variant or a usage resource.
notes: SOURCE FACT; historical ISO 9241 origin relation is explicit.

locator: ISO OBP preview, table of contents, introduction and §1
evidence_summary: ISO/IEC 25063 structures a context-of-use description around user population, user/organization goals and responsibilities, user tasks, user environments and problems; it specifies content elements but no particular documentation layout or method.
limitations: Normative detailed element definitions and checklist are not publicly accessible in the preview.

locator: ISO landing page — abstract and life-cycle relation to ISO/IEC 25010:2011
evidence_summary: ISO/IEC 25019:2023 defines a quality-in-use model for products or systems used in a specified context of use, and says context of use is a prerequisite that must be re-specified if the context a product or service is intended to fulfil changes. ISO identifies it as the current successor to the quality-in-use part of withdrawn ISO/IEC 25010:2011.
limitations: The public abstract does not supply a claim-level comparison rule or a full set of quality-in-use subcharacteristics.

evidence_summary: CISU-R separates a usability requirement into context of use, performance/satisfaction criteria, and a test method; the test-method part can identify the context in which measurements will be made and can grow into a complete test protocol.
limitations: A 2007 NIST methodology based on then-current standards; it is not a general product-review conflict standard.

evidence_summary: Maguire describes context of use as the goals of the user community and the main user, task and environmental characteristics of the situation in which a product will operate, and presents context analysis as preceding usability design or evaluation.
limitations: Only publisher metadata and abstract were accessible; the paper's detailed process is not asserted here.

evidence_summary: Alonso-Ríos et al. propose a detailed taxonomy because context characteristics were often overlooked and no sufficiently detailed model was available; their taxonomy separates users, tasks and environments and describes physical, social and technical environment branches.
supports: taxonomy is a proposal not a standard
limitations: This is one 2010 proposed taxonomy, not an ISO taxonomy or a universal field inventory; detailed locator was read through a same-origin mirror.
notes: SOURCE FACT; mirror is not an additional source.

evidence_summary: The proposed taxonomy treats role, knowledge/experience and physical characteristics as user attributes; it includes task temporal characteristics such as duration and frequency, and distinguishes physical, social and technical environmental factors. It cautions that usability results from one context cannot be directly generalized to other contexts.
limitations: Taxonomy definitions and the non-generalization claim are author proposals/interpretations within one study, not an ISO-mandated schema or a formal conflict rule.
notes: SOURCE FACT about the paper's taxonomy and stated limitation.

evidence_summary: Dey defines context as information that characterizes the situation of an entity; an entity can be a relevant person, place or object in an interaction between a user and an application. Relevance is situation-dependent rather than a fixed enumerated list.
limitations: Context-aware computing formulation; it does not define product-review entities, usability dimensions or a controlled review taxonomy.

evidence_summary: Dey's toolkit stores sensed context, uses interpreters to produce context from one or more context inputs, and defines a situation as a description of relevant entities' states; the paper explicitly notes a trade-off between supporting very complex situations and a simple description method.
limitations: The architecture concerns sensed application context. It supplies no rule for inferring unspoken usage conditions from product-review prose or for assigning inference confidence.

evidence_summary: Dey, Salber and Abowd introduce four essential context-information characteristics: identity, location, status (or activity), and time, with expanded descriptions rather than a universal closed ontology.
limitations: The categories were developed for context-aware applications and do not cover ISO's full user-goal-task-resource-environment structure; status/activity is not automatically an R03 product-system-state field.

evidence_summary: The framework says interpreters raise the abstraction level by transforming one or more context sources into new context information, while aggregators collect logically related context for an entity.
limitations: A software architecture pattern, not evidence that an LLM or annotator may infer an unstated review condition as fact.

evidence_summary: The paper notes that sensed context is not always accurate, distinguishes automatic and manual disambiguation, and proposes providing context with a measure of accuracy when an infrastructure can meet a requested accuracy.
limitations: It concerns sensor-acquired context rather than textual extraction confidence or evidence reliability of a review author.

locator: pp. 39–46, §8.4 context attributes and quality-of-service requirements
evidence_summary: The framework treats context attributes as entity-relative and separately specifies requirements such as coverage, resolution, accuracy, reliability, update frequency and timeliness for dynamically acquired context.
limitations: These are sensing/service-quality requirements, not a product-test protocol and not evidence that all product review claims need these fields.

locator: PROV-Overview abstract and PROV family description
evidence_summary: The W3C PROV family describes provenance as information about entities, activities and people involved in producing data or things, intended to support assessments of quality, reliability or trustworthiness; it includes attribution, processing steps and derivation concepts.
limitations: PROV is not a context-of-use taxonomy, an uncertainty calculus, or a review-annotation standard.

locator: Chapter 6, “Defining Opportunities and Context of Use,” Figure 6-2 discussion
evidence_summary: The National Research Council frames context of use as including users' characteristics, motivations, goals and strategies; activities and tasks; communication and collaboration patterns; and physical, technical, organizational and political environments that create opportunities and constraints on performance.
limitations: A 2007 human-system-integration framework; its broad list does not prescribe a universal review data model or distinguish product variant from use context.

evidence_summary: PROV distinguishes an entity derived from another entity and can qualify derivation with an activity, generation and usage; more specific provenance relations are available when applicable.
limitations: This supports recording derivation provenance in principle only; it does not determine whether a contextual inference is correct or how confident an NLP system should be.
